name: Spondyloepimetaphyseal Dysplasia-Abnormal Dentition Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for SEMD-Abnormal Dentition Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia features including abnormalities of spine, epiphyses, and metaphyses on radiographs
Abnormal dentition characterized by enamel hypoplasia, delayed tooth eruption, and malformed teeth
Clinical evidence of disproportionate short-trunk dwarfism
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated genes (e.g., COL2A1 or other related genes)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: characteristic skeletal abnormalities, abnormal dentition, and short-trunk dwarfism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical and radiological features are primary.

pathognomonic.notes: Radiologically evident abnormalities in spine, epiphyses, and metaphyses
searchTerms: skeletal dysplasia affecting spine and joints

pathognomonic.notes: Clinically evident short stature with trunk shortening

common.notes: Conductive or sensorineural hearing loss reported
Midface hypoplasia and flattened nasal bridge

occasional.notes: Degenerative joint disease secondary to skeletal abnormalities
Restrictive lung disease due to thoracic deformities

searchTerms: growth hormone deficiency causing short height

rare.notes: Mild mitral or aortic valve involvement

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to spinal cord compression

laboratory: Possible mild elevation of alkaline phosphatase related to bone turnover
imaging: Radiographs showing spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia with platyspondyly, metaphyseal irregularities, and epiphyseal abnormalities
Spinal MRI for evaluation of cord compression or atlantoaxial instability
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COL2A1 or other collagen-related genes implicated in skeletal dysplasias
other: Dental examination revealing enamel hypoplasia and malformed teeth

distinguishingFeatures: More pronounced epiphyseal involvement without metaphyseal changes
Different genetic mutations (COL2A1 variants distinct from SEMD-AD)
Severe short stature with characteristic facial features
Dental abnormalities but with systemic bone mineralization defects

redFlags: Severe respiratory insufficiency due to thoracic deformities
Rapidly worsening joint deformities or early-onset osteoarthritis
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasias. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
